page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.8xlarge is an x86_64 server instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz, supported by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 33 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, resulting in an exact 1:1 ratio of 1.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance includes 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and provides zero GPUs.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily within average performance tiers for its hardware tier. It records a Geekbench single-core score of 1439.0 and a multi-core score of 12692.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 34140.29. In memory testing, large block read throughput reaches 154.63 GB/sec and write bandwidth measures 69.38 GB/sec. For compression and text processing, it scores 27.7 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 161.14 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The instance demonstrates strong text generation on small 135M language models at 304.01 tokens/sec, while medium 7B model text generation yields an average 18.54 tokens/sec.

The 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio marks a significant architectural tradeoff, offering high core parallelism but constrained memory per thread compared to typical 1:2 or 1:4 general-purpose standards. The absence of integrated local storage necessitates network-attached volumes for data retention. This resource profile delivers compute density suited for CPU-bound multi-threaded tasks that do not consume large memory footprints, such as CI/CD software compilation, static web serving, compute-heavy batch processing, and microservice workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.8xlarge is an x86_64 instance featuring 32 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs (16 physical cores) operating at 2.5 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of memory for a 1:1 core-to-RAM balance. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor, includes 10 Gbps baseline networking, and features no dedicated local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance shows steady middle-tier multi-threaded capacity, scoring 34140.29 in PassMark CPU tests and 12692.0 in Geekbench multi-core, with a strong output of 304.01 tokens/sec on small 135M model text generation. Because memory is limited to 1.0 GB per vCPU and local storage is absent, it is poorly suited for in-memory databases but well matched for parallel compute jobs, Clang software builds, static web servers, and distributed microservices.
